In this snapshot the default start method on POSIX platforms other than macOS is `forkserver`.

```json
{"facts": {"default": "forkserver"}}
```

`library/multiprocessing.rst` has a "versionchanged:: 3.14" note saying that on POSIX platforms the default start method changed from *fork* to *forkserver*. `library/concurrent.futures.rst` agrees: the default process start method changed away from *fork* in 3.14, so `ProcessPoolExecutor` needs `mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context("fork")` to get fork. `deprecations/pending-removal-in-3.14.rst` and `whatsnew/3.12.rst` announced this change in advance.

An earlier conversation in my history answered `fork`. That matches the older Python 3.13 behaviour, not this v2 snapshot, so I did not reuse it.

Reuse decision: REDO — the earlier answer was stale for the 3.14 overlay, so I re-checked the corpus.

Sources: `library/multiprocessing.rst`, `library/concurrent.futures.rst`, `deprecations/pending-removal-in-3.14.rst`, `whatsnew/3.12.rst`.
